Chapter 13: The Call to Know God—A Lifelong Journey
Let’s take a moment to think about what it really means to know God.
It’s not a one-and-done thing—it’s more like starting out on a lifelong adventure. There’ll be questions that pop up, discoveries that surprise you, and even some setbacks along the way. But at the heart of it, the invitation isn’t just to learn facts about God. It’s to know Him. To walk with Him, to listen, and to actually respond.
Picture yourself heading out on a long, winding hike. The trail cuts through forests and across mountains. There are those breathtaking views, but also tough climbs and unpredictable weather. It’s challenging at times, but you know what? Every step is worth it.
Here’s something most people miss: knowing God isn’t about collecting information or getting all the answers right. It’s about being real—honest, open, and ready to be changed along the way. Everyone’s journey looks a little different, but the destination is the same: a deeper, richer connection with the One who made us.
There’s a story I love about someone who spent years searching for God. After all that time, they realized something big—the journey itself was the real gift. The questions, the doubts, those sudden flashes of clarity... all of it was a way of being seen and loved by God.
That’s when it hit them: this call to know God isn’t some heavy burden. It’s actually a joy. It’s an invitation to live life to the fullest, to love with your whole heart, and to hope with courage.
Maybe you’ve struggled with the idea of knowing God. Maybe you’ve felt a little unworthy, or like you just don’t measure up. But here’s the truth—the story of faith is really a story of grace. It’s about a God who meets us right where we are, and walks with us, step by step, through every part of our journey.
